newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Accord reach with Portugal striking miners - company.
newsitem.headline: Accord reach with Portugal striking miners - company.

text.p: State-run Somincor has reached agreement with striking miners at the Neves Corvo copper mine which should permit a return to work, company president Alcides Pereira told Reuters on Saturday.

Pereira, whose company controls the mine, said a deal had been reached with strike leaders after marathon talks on Friday night. The accord still has to be put to a vote by striking miners by their leaders, he said.
"The unions accepted our proposal in principle...I hope full production will resume on Monday," he said.
Workers at the mine, 250 km south of Lisbon, went on strike on Monday in protest over company plans to introduce Sunday shifts.
Their action had brought output at the 107,000 tonnes per year mine to a complete standstill.
Government representatives had joined leaders of the miners' unions and management at the talks in nearby Beja on Friday in an attempt to break the deadlock.
Eduardo Lazaro, a director of the miners' union, confirmed to Reuters that a deal had been reached.
Workers would be meeting either overnight or on Saturday to vote on the accord and providing that it was approved, work would resume on Monday, he said.
"I think that it will be accepted by my colleagues," he told Reuters.
The accord calls for the company to send a proposal for continuous working, including Sunday shifts, at the mine by next Wednesday.
The proposal "would meet some of the demands of the workers," Lazaro said, without giving full details.
Pereira said that he was also optmistic that the workers would accept the proposals and that production would be resumed in full.
